summary: Rebuilt M3-S03 (Email-to-Case routing addresses, Web-to-Case intake, Case settings) retested clean after the F-25/F-26/F-27 fix. Declared build-scope checker check_case_management_setup.py exits 0; the always-on XML (2/2 parse) and manifest (Settings:Case consistent) checks pass; check-outputs ok. Two manual tests deferred to the milestone gate, both well-formed Given/When/Then with named observable outcomes. Step moved built -> tested.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed (step-tester Plan Step 7 HIGH condition).

process_observations.observation: The declared checker (build scope, check_case_management_setup.py) exits 0 on the rebuilt artefacts and its cross-file assertion (webToCase.caseOrigin against M1-S01's CaseOrigin standardValueSet) is satisfiable at this scope, unlike the pre-rebuild run whose defects only the org's own validation caught.

The manifest declares Settings:Case explicitly rather than a wildcard, matching case-management-setup section 5's documented rule that the wildcard does not apply to feature settings, and both manifest directions resolve one-to-one.

check_email_to_case_configuration.py is not declared on this step by design, and it now carries three new rules from today's commit 0b8805803 (E2C-RT-01, E2C-RT-02, E2C-PRI-01) that this test run never exercises against these artefacts.

Manual test 4 says the webToCase block carries exactly its three documented children while also saying defaultResponseTemplate is deliberately unset, but the file carries only two of the three documented children.
build-doc-keeper should run next now that M3-S03 is tested, to update PLAN.md, the workbook and traceability against the rebuilt artefacts.
process_observations.followup_reason: The step just moved built -> tested and the doc keeper is the next stage of the build loop for a tested step.

process_observations.observation: milestone-verifier should run once the remaining M3 steps (M3-S04, M3-S05) reach documented, against these rebuilt artefacts rather than the pre-rebuild ones.

skipped_manual: Given check_email_to_case_configuration.py is not declared here (see the step note), when settings/Case.settings-meta.xml is read, then both routing addresses carry their own caseOrigin (Email-Support, Email-Billing) and no caseOwner, unauthorizedSenderAction is Bounce, overEmailLimitAction is Requeue, saveEmailHeaders is true on both, and the webToCase block carries exactly its three documented children — enableWebToCase true and a caseOrigin that is a live CaseOrigin value from M1-S01, with defaultResponseTemplate deliberately unset because the guide scopes it to Self-Service portal responses rather than to the customer acknowledgement, which is M3-S04's auto-response rule.

Given Q66's answer itself says to confirm how the website form posts, when web-to-case-form-contract.md is read, then it states whether the form posts directly to Web-to-Case or through middleware, the Origin value each path stamps, and — per case-management-setup § 4 — that the HTML form itself is not metadata and has no metadata type, so it is authored and hosted outside this build.
